Chapter Four: Moving Beyond the Expectation That Hard Work Alone Will Be Rewarded.
Let’s be honest—most of us grew up believing that if we just work hard enough, people will notice, and the rewards will follow. Sound familiar? That idea usually starts in school, where effort and results go hand in hand—and a gold star or a good grade comes right after you put in the work. Even early in our careers, this pattern often holds true. But as you move up, things get more complicated. The connection between how hard you work and the recognition you receive isn't always so clear.
In today’s organizations, it’s usually the most visible people—the ones who make their contributions known—who get picked for promotions or exciting new projects. Don’t get me wrong; hard work still matters. But it’s just one piece of a much bigger puzzle. If you really want to move forward, you’ll need more than just effort. You need visibility, good communication, and strong relationships.
Think of it like this: Imagine you have a beautiful garden. You spend hours watering, planting, and weeding. But if your garden’s hidden behind a tall fence, no one else will ever see how amazing it is. Opening the gate—letting people in to appreciate what you’ve done—is just as important as tending the plants.
When we expect that hard work alone will get us noticed, it can actually lead to disappointment. You might find yourself working harder and harder, wondering why no one seems to recognize your efforts. That frustration can quickly lead to burnout, especially if you’re piling on more and more tasks in the hope that someone will finally see just how much you’re doing. It’s an exhausting cycle, and it’s tough to break out of it unless you consciously decide to change your approach.
So, how do you move beyond this habit? Here are a few things to focus on:
First, recognize that being visible really matters. It’s not just about doing great work—it’s about making sure the right people know about it. Next, practice communicating your contributions and results, especially to those who make decisions about promotions or new opportunities. Find ways to showcase what you’re working on. That might mean giving a short presentation, sharing a project update, or even just sending a friendly email to highlight a recent success. And don’t forget to build relationships with the folks who have a say in your career growth. Having supporters and advocates can make all the difference.
Now, this doesn’t mean you should stop working hard. But it does mean you’ll want to balance that effort with smart, strategic actions that boost your visibility and influence. That way, you’re not just hoping your work will be noticed—you’re making sure of it.
There’s another piece to this puzzle, too. Sometimes, it’s easy to get so caught up in your daily to-do list that you forget about your long-term goals. Ever find yourself just putting out fires, day after day, with no time left to think about where you actually want to go? Taking a step back to reflect on your bigger career aspirations is essential if you want to keep growing.
Here are some practical ways to line up your daily work with those long-term goals:
Make it a habit to review your career objectives and check in on your progress. Ask for feedback and advice from a mentor or sponsor—they can help you spot opportunities you might have missed. Look for ways to stretch yourself, like joining a new project or signing up for extra training. And be proactive. Don’t wait for challenges to come to you—seek them out.
When you put these ideas into practice, you’ll find it’s possible to move past the old belief that hard work alone will bring rewards. Instead, you’ll be actively shaping your career, building new skills, and creating opportunities for yourself—one intentional step at a time.
